in_text_mentions: During the follow-up, eight (89%) patients had ophthalmologic manifestations. The main symptoms were scotoma and blurred vision. Branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO), the most characteristic ophthalmologic lesion in retinal FA or OCT-A, was found in eight (89%) patients (Figure 2A,B). One patient had no ocular symptoms but presented BRAO on ophthalmological exam. In seven patients, ocular involvement was bilateral. In four cases (44%), signs of arteriolar vasculitis were also present (Figure 2C). At the end of follow-up, four out of the nine patients had ocular damage (Table 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: OCT panel (fundus image plus B-scan with ILM/RPE/choroid labels) from a Susac syndrome case showing widening of the inner retinal layer signifying retinal edema, the OCT correlate of the central retinal artery branch occlusion confirmed on fluorescein angiography in the same eye; branch retinal artery occlusion with retinal edema is a classic ophthalmic manifestation of Susac syndrome. b: Right-eye visual field grayscale plot showing a central scotoma, the functional correlate of the branch retinal artery occlusion in this Susac syndrome case; the scotoma and the OCT retinal edema are the classic ophthalmic manifestations of the disease in this patient.

Fluorescein angiography of the right eye disclosed central retinal artery branch occlusion. The patient was treated with Aspirin. At this point of time, workup also included negative studies for hypercoagulopathy, negative serological studies for antinuclear factor, anti DNA antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Real axial T2 FLAIR brain MRI from a Susac syndrome case. Caption and in-text describe hyperintense lesions in the cerebellar hemispheres, periventricular white matter and leptomeninges, all part of the encephalopathic presentation of Susac syndrome. No provided vocabulary key covers cerebellar or leptomeningeal lesions, so these are recorded as proposed_findings; the panel is retained because the manifestation is named and the disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused title plus the caption. b: Axial T2 FLAIR MRI showing a bright central corpus callosum lesion; the caption explicitly calls these 'snowball lesions' in the body of the corpus callosum, the hallmark MRI finding of Susac syndrome, and the article title and in-text confirm corpus callosum involvement in a Susac patient. High-confidence classic manifestation.

Extensive postcontrast T2 FLAIR enhancement of periventricular and cerebellar diseases with patchy leptomeningeal enhancement accentuated by the FLAIR technique. (a) Large T2 FLAIR signal in the body of corpus (snowball lesions) and throughout the periventricular white matter. (b) Regions of T2 FLAIR signal correlated with DWI (b1000) diffusion restriction.
